pr_body:
/kind bug
/kind cleanup

Fixes #100849

Add a function ` func CloseIdleConnectionsFor(transport http.RoundTripper) `  that allow to close the idle connections that belong to the transport, if the transport implements the `RoundTripperWrapper` interface.

Use this new function to close the idle connections on kubelet and avoid using a custom dialer that forces the kubelet to create multiple TCP connections , instead of reusing a single one.

```release-note
Don't use a custom dialer for the kubelet if is not rotating certificates, so we can reuse TCP connections and have only one between the apiserver and the kubelet.
If users experiment problems with stale connections  using HTTP1.1, they can force the previous behavior of the kubelet by setting the environment variable DISABLE_HTTP2.
```

> @liggitt since the only case we have doubts is with HTTP1.1, and we already have an environment variable to DISABLE_HTTP2, users can force the previous behavior setting this variable

is that correct? `DISABLE_HTTP2` can force use of http/1.1, but if there's an issue with http/1.1, there's no way to force http/2, right?

The scenario I'm thinking of is a kubelet talking to a http/1.1 load balancer, where http/2 is not an option, regardless of the envvar. Load balancer-fronted API servers were exactly the scenario I remember being most problematic around the kubelet getting perma-stuck connections.

> is that correct? `DISABLE_HTTP2` can force use of http/1.1, but if there's an issue with http/1.1, there's no way to force http/2, right?

HTTP2 is enabled by default, 

https://github.com/aojea/kubernetes/blob/90918a0a873f068b8be5d1e08f7eee8054d9c36e/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/net/http.go#L125-L151

if they have http/1.1 has to be because they have some intermediate proxy, L4 loadbalancers are transparent.

> Load balancer-fronted API servers were exactly the scenario I remember being most problematic around the kubelet getting perma-stuck connections.

Yeah, this is the typical setup with nginx as reverse proxies, indeed is the more complex because there are a lot of points of failures, not only the network, users need to handle the certificates on the proxies too, ...

If something happens related to stuck connections it has to be http1.1 (or we have a new bug in http2). Since this env variable is documented, I just added it to recover previous behavior when closing the connections, in case that the new CloseIdleConnections() doesn't work (we don't have evidence yet)

> If something happens related to stuck connections it has to be http1.1 (or we have a new bug in http2). Since this env variable is documented, I just added it to recover previous behavior when closing the connections, in case that the new CloseIdleConnections() doesn't work (we don't have evidence yet)

I see... so the expectation would be:

1. kubelets using http/2 would use the http/2 ping timeout and this CloseIdleConnections mechanism
2. kubelets that automatically negotiated back to http/1.1 would use only this CloseIdleConnections mechanism
3. a kubelet could be forced to use http/1.1 and use the old tear-down-all-connections mechanism by explicitly setting DISABLE_HTTP2

That limits the exposure to regressions because of this new mechanism without an escape hatch to kubelets which:
1. don't use client certificate rotation
2. use http/2

That seems reasonable to me, though I'd like a sig-node reviewer to ack as well.
